name: SG90 Micro Servo (180°)
desc: A small motor that turns to an exact angle (0–180°) and holds it. Use it for flags, pointers, locks and robot arms.
power: One SG90 can run from the board's 5V pin for testing. For two or more, use a separate 5V supply and connect its GND to the board's GND.

name: MG996R Metal-Gear Servo
desc: A big, strong servo with metal gears for heavy jobs like robot legs, steering and doors.
power: MG996R can pull over 2A when it strains. Always give it its own 5–6V supply (2A or more) and connect GND to the board. Never power it from the board.

name: 28BYJ-48 5V Stepper Motor
desc: A geared motor that moves in tiny exact steps (about 2048 per turn). Slow but precise: perfect for clocks, turntables and dials.
power: 28BYJ-48 must be driven through a ULN2003 driver board, never straight from pins. It draws ~240mA, so a separate 5V supply is best.

name: ULN2003 Stepper Driver Board
desc: The little driver board that comes with the 28BYJ-48. It lets 4 weak board pins switch the motor's coils, with protection diodes built in.

name: TT Gear Motor (yellow, 3–6V)
desc: The yellow geared motor used in most robot car kits. Slow and strong enough to drive wheels.
power: Never connect a TT motor to a board pin. Drive it with a motor driver (L298N, TB6612FNG) or a transistor plus a flyback diode, from a separate battery.

name: 130 DC Hobby Motor
desc: A small, fast spinning motor for fans, spinners and propellers. It spins fast but has little force.
power: Never connect a DC motor to a board pin. Use a transistor/MOSFET plus a flyback diode (1N4007), or a motor driver, with a separate supply.

name: L298N Dual Motor Driver
desc: Controls the speed and direction of two DC motors (or one stepper). The classic, sturdy robot-car driver.
power: L298N needs a separate battery for the motors (6–12V; it loses about 2V inside). Connect its GND to the board's GND. Protection diodes are on the board.
note: Keep the 5V-EN jumper on only when the motor supply is 12V or less.

name: TB6612FNG Dual Motor Driver
desc: A small, efficient driver for two DC motors. It wastes far less power than the L298N and works with 3.3V boards.
power: Motors get their own supply on VM. Connect all GNDs together. The STBY pin must be HIGH or nothing moves.
note: Usually ships with loose header pins that need soldering.

name: Coin Vibration Motor
desc: The flat buzzing motor from phones. Adds a rumble to controllers, alarms and wearables.
power: Even this small motor draws ~80mA. Switch it with a transistor (2N2222 + 1kΩ) and put a 1N4007 flyback diode across it.

name: Mini Submersible Water Pump (3–5V)
desc: A tiny pump that sits in water and pushes it through a tube. Use it for auto-watering plants or a drink dispenser.
power: Never connect the pump to a board pin. Switch it with a logic-level MOSFET or transistor plus a flyback diode, ideally from a separate 5V supply. Keep water away from the electronics.

name: MG90S Metal-Gear Micro Servo
desc: Same size as the SG90 but with tougher metal gears. Better for small robot arms.
power: One MG90S on the board's 5V pin is OK for testing; for several, use a separate 5V supply and connect GNDs.

name: Continuous Rotation Servo (FS90R)
desc: A servo that spins all the way around instead of going to an angle. write(90) stops it; lower/higher = direction and speed.
power: For more than one, use a separate 5V supply and connect GNDs.

name: DS3218 20kg Digital Servo
desc: A very strong servo for big robot joints and steering.
power: Can draw 2–3A under load. Always give it its own 5–6V supply (3A+) and connect GND to the board.

name: NEMA 17 Stepper Motor (bipolar)
desc: The precise, strong stepper used in 3D printers: 200 steps per turn, lots of torque.
power: Needs an A4988 or DRV8825 driver and a 12V supply. Set the driver's current limit before first use.

name: A4988 Stepper Driver
desc: A small board that runs a NEMA 17 stepper with just two pins: STEP and DIR.
power: Put a 100µF capacitor across VMOT/GND, set the current limit with its tiny screw, and never unplug the motor while powered.

name: DRV8825 Stepper Driver
desc: Like the A4988 but handles more current and higher voltage, with finer microstepping.
power: Put a 100µF capacitor across VMOT/GND, set the current limit first, and never unplug the motor while powered.

name: N20 Micro Gear Motor (6V)
desc: A tiny metal-geared motor: strong for its size, ideal for small robots.
power: Never connect it to a board pin. Use a motor driver (DRV8833, TB6612FNG) with its own battery.

name: DRV8833 Dual Motor Driver
desc: A small, efficient driver for two small DC motors (or one stepper). Works great with 3.3V boards.
power: Motors get their own supply on VM; connect all GNDs together.

name: L9110S Dual Motor Driver
desc: A very cheap driver for two small DC motors (up to ~0.8A each). Speed via PWM on the inputs.
power: Motors are powered through the driver from a battery, never from board pins. Connect GNDs.

name: BTS7960 43A Motor Driver
desc: A heavy-duty driver for big 12V motors: go-karts, ride-on cars, big robots.
power: Big motors can draw tens of amps: use thick wires, an inline fuse and a suitable battery. Connect GNDs.

name: PCA9685 16-Channel Servo Driver (I2C)
desc: Controls up to 16 servos with just 2 wires. The secret behind most robot arms and spiders.
power: Servos get their power from the screw terminal (5–6V, enough amps for all of them), never from the board.

name: 5V Brushless Fan (40mm)
desc: A small cooling fan for enclosures and soldering-fume extractors.
power: Switch it with a transistor/MOSFET (a flyback diode is still good practice), not straight from a pin.

name: 12V PC Fan (80mm)
desc: A quiet, strong 12V computer fan for cooling boxes and air purifiers.
power: Needs a 12V supply switched with a logic-level MOSFET. Connect the 12V supply's GND to the board's GND.

name: 12V Push-Pull Solenoid
desc: An electromagnet that shoots a metal pin out (or pulls it in). Door latches, button pushers, drum hits!
power: Needs a 12V supply, a logic-level MOSFET and a flyback diode (1N4007). Only short pulses: it gets hot if held on.

name: Vibration Motor Module (with driver)
desc: A coin vibration motor on a little board that already has the transistor and diode. The safe, easy way to add rumble.

name: 2WD Robot Car Chassis Kit
desc: An acrylic chassis with 2 TT gear motors, wheels, a caster wheel and a 4×AA holder: the body of your first robot.
power: Drive the motors through an L298N or TB6612FNG, never from board pins.
